content: A dedicated pelvic MRI protocol is recommended for optimal evaluation of pelvic pathology. MRI is considered superior to CT for local staging of pelvic tumors. The use of contrast-enhanced MRI improves the accuracy of detecting myometrial invasion. On T1-weighted imaging, the tumor appears hypoto isointense compared to the normal endometrium. On T1-weighted imaging with contrast (Gadolinium), carcinomatous tissue enhances less than the normal endometrium. On T2-weighted imaging, the tumor appears hyperintense or heterogeneous relative to the normal endometrium. MRI findings based on FIGO staging are as follows: Stage 1: Tumor confined to the uterus. Stage 1a: Tumor is confined to the uterine endometrium. The endometrium may appear normal or widened. The junctional zone shows a normal low T2 signal. Complete subendometrial enhancement is observed on T1 contrast imaging. Stage 1b: Tumor invades less than half of the myometrium. There is disruption or irregularity of the low T2 signal junctional zone. Subendometrial early enhancement is disrupted. Stage 1c: Tumor invades the outer half of the myometrium. Disruption or irregularity of the low T2 signal junctional zone is noted. Subendometrial early enhancement is disrupted. A band of the outer myometrium is preserved. Stage 2: Tumor extends to the cervix. Stage 2a: There is widening of the internal os and endocervical canal due to a tumor mass with high or isointense T2-weighted signal.
